betaLB: Example Using the DiffBetaLB Function

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Source: vignettes/example-diff-beta-lb.Rmd
example-diff-beta-lb.Rmd

In this example, a multiple regression model is fitted using program quality ratings (QUALITY) as the regressand/outcome variable and number of published articles attributed to the program faculty members (NARTIC), percent of faculty members holding research grants (PCTGRT), and percentage of program graduates who received support (PCTSUPP) as regressor/predictor variables using a data set from 1982 ratings of 46 doctoral programs in psychology in the USA (National Research Council, 1982).

library(package = betaLB)
df <- betaLB::nas1982

Fit the regression model using the lm() function. 

object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)

Estimate the standardized regression slopes.

DiffBetaLB() needs fully standardized slopes (std_y = TRUE and std_x = NULL).

std <- BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))

Differences of standardized slopes

The likelihood intervals of the differences \beta^{\ast}_{i} - \beta^{\ast}_{j} are solved for every pair of regressors.

diff <- DiffBetaLB(object = std, alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))
summary(object = diff, alpha = 0.05)
#> Call:
#> DiffBetaLB(object = std, alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))
#> 
#> Differences of standardized regression slopes with ROBUST likelihood intervals:
#>                     est    2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC - PCTGRT  0.1037 -0.1345 0.3358
#> NARTIC - PCTSUPP 0.2319 -0.0040 0.4557
#> PCTGRT - PCTSUPP 0.1282 -0.1118 0.3623
coef(object = diff)
#>  NARTIC - PCTGRT NARTIC - PCTSUPP PCTGRT - PCTSUPP 
#>        0.1036564        0.2318974        0.1282410
confint(object = diff, level = 0.99)
#>                        0.5 %    99.5 %
#> NARTIC - PCTGRT  -0.21026750 0.4074141
#> NARTIC - PCTSUPP -0.08126166 0.5244509
#> PCTGRT - PCTSUPP -0.18999595 0.4361053

References

Dudgeon, P. (2017). Some improvements in confidence intervals for standardized regression coefficients. Psychometrika, 82(4), 928–951. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11336-017-9563-z
National Research Council. (1982). An assessment of research-doctorate programs in the United States: Social and behavioral sciences. National Academies Press. https://doi.org/10.17226/9781
